_about: Real lander/rover catalog for the Mission tab (checked 2026-11-15). Every value is { value, isReference, origin, from }: origin 'published' = official spec (source in the vehicle's sources); 'estimate' = not published, derived from a documented figure (the 'from' text says which and how); 'reference' = nothing documented, default value of the app or of a comparable vehicle ('from' says which). isReference is true for 'estimate' and 'reference': the interface flags them. Every value is editable.

userInputs.dailyNeedKWh: energy to collect per day (kWh/day), same as the Mission tab row 'Energy to collect per day'

mappingToEnergyJs.consumption: { operatingW: dailyNeedKWh * 1000 / 24, survivalW: 0, operatingHoursPerDay: 24 }  -> neededWhPerDay = dailyNeedKWh * 1000
mappingToEnergyJs.batteryWh: the vehicle's batteryWh when official, else null

energyModel.derivingAreaFromWatts: when a maker publishes peak panel power P (W): panelAreaM2 = P / (1361 * efficiency), with 1361 W/m2 the solar constant already used in energy.js

references._why: Values used when no official spec exists (isReference=true).

panelEfficiencyPct.source: Spectrolab XTJ Prime datasheet: 30.7% at beginning of life, 26.7% at end of life; 28 is also the Generic lander's value

dailyNeedKWhLander.source: Generic lander of the app: 200 W x 8 h + 30 W x 16 h

dailyNeedKWhRover.source: VIPER hibernation floor: 5,420 Wh / 50 h = 108 W, x 24 h (NASA, Feb 2025)

driveSlopeMaxDeg.source: VIPER nominal drive slope (NASA), used for rovers without a published value

landers.name: Griffin

panelAreaM2.from: Generic lander of the app (2 m2)

panelEfficiencyPct.from: Space solar cells, Spectrolab XTJ Prime data sheet: 30.7% new, 26.7% end of life

dailyNeedKWh.from: Generic lander of the app: 200 W x 8 h + 30 W x 16 h = 2.08 kWh

notes: Landing sites are selected with an effective slope of 10 deg or less; landing ellipse 100 m x 100 m; direct-to-Earth X-band link (Astrobotic user guide).
Energy: Astrobotic gives 1 W per kg of payload (625 W for a full load), so the array is at least 625 / (1361 x 0.28) = 1.64 m2; the reference 2 m2 is consistent with that.
Landing sequence: the guide mentions a 2 h powered descent; kept at the app default until the team decides.

Not used as estimates (kept at the reference), see the guide: payload data 10 kbps per kg (6,250 kbps for 625 kg, more than the app's X-band class and only while payloads are attached); data service about 7 h per 8 h cycle on the surface (ground station switching, not a need); the thermal range excludes the lunar night (Griffin is not designed to survive it, no figure).

sources.label: Astrobotic, Lunar Landers Payload User's Guide v5.0 (Aug 2021)

landers.name: Blue Moon MK1

landingAccuracyM.from: Blue Origin's goal for the MK1 pathfinder: precision landing within 100 m

notes: Payload up to 3 metric tons (Blue Origin).

energy = null on purpose: MK1 runs on an oxygen/hydrogen fuel cell (plus Power Towers > 10 kW), which the solar model cannot represent. The interface should say 'not solar: not modeled' instead of prefilling.
Carries VIPER (MK1-102) and the two Lunar Terrain Vehicles (MK1-103, MK1-104).

landers.name: Nova-C

survivalHours.from: IM-1 (Odysseus): IM engineers expected 10 to 20 h of link after sunset on the battery; low end kept (Wikipedia, Nova-C)

antenna.from: S-band link to Intuitive Machines' Lunar Data Network (intuitivemachines.com/im-2): medium-gain class

panelAreaM2.from: 200 W peak from 3 panels (Wikipedia, Nova-C): 200 / (1361 x 0.28) = 0.52 m2

panelEfficiencyPct.from: Space solar cells, Spectrolab XTJ Prime data sheet: 30.7% new, 26.7% end of life

dailyNeedKWh.from: Generic lander of the app: 200 W x 8 h + 30 W x 16 h = 2.08 kWh

notes: Payload > 130 kg and landing on slopes up to 10 deg (Intuitive Machines, LPSC 2024).

Energy estimate from an unofficial source (Wikipedia): 200 W peak from 3 panels, so area = 200 / (1361 x 0.28) = 0.52 m2. Survival estimate: 10 h, low end of the 10-20 h of link after sunset IM expected for IM-1.

landers.name: Blue Ghost

antenna.from: One X-band antenna and three S-band antennas on Blue Ghost Mission 1 (Vulcan Wireless, supplier, via SatNews): high-gain X-band class

panelAreaM2.from: 400 W peak from 3 panels (Firefly): 400 / (1361 x 0.28) = 1.05 m2

panelEfficiencyPct.from: Space solar cells, Spectrolab XTJ Prime data sheet: 30.7% new, 26.7% end of life

dailyNeedKWh.from: Generic lander of the app: 200 W x 8 h + 30 W x 16 h = 2.08 kWh

notes: Payload up to 240 kg; link direct-to-Earth or through a relay (Firefly).
Survival: just over 5 hours of operations into the lunar night (Mission 1, Firefly).
Energy: 400 W peak from 3 panels (Firefly), so area = 400 / (1361 x 0.28) = 1.05 m2 (estimate, isReference).

sources.label: SatNews, Vulcan Wireless on Blue Ghost Mission 1 communications (Mar 2025)

landers.name: Starship HLS
notes: Slope: NASA requirement, landing surface slope under 10 deg over 100 m; direct-with-Earth link, no relay assumed (NASA HLS update 2024).
energy = null on purpose: no official power figures, and the reference values (2 m2, 2 kWh/day) would be meaningless for a 50 m crewed ship. The interface should say 'not published'.

rovers.name: VIPER

panelAreaM2.from: 450 W from the corner-facing array (NASA, Feb 2025): 450 / (1361 x 0.28) = 1.18 m2

panelEfficiencyPct.from: Space solar cells, Spectrolab XTJ Prime data sheet: 30.7% new, 26.7% end of life

dailyNeedKWh.from: VIPER hibernation floor (NASA, Feb 2025): 5,420 Wh battery / 50 h = 108 W, x 24 h = 2.6 kWh; the need while driving is higher

notes: Mass 450 kg; X-band direct-to-Earth over the Deep Space Network; drive slope up to 15 deg normally, 25-30 deg when necessary (NASA).
Energy, official: 450 W from a corner-facing array (320 W per array), battery 5,420 Wh, 9 h of shadowed operations or 50 h of hibernation on the battery (NASA, Feb 2025).
Energy, estimates: area = 450 / (1361 x 0.28) = 1.18 m2; daily need 2.6 kWh = hibernation floor (108 W x 24 h), the real need while driving is higher.

Survival: 96 h, the mission limit of NASA's lunar operations page (darkness longer than four Earth days ends the mission). The Feb 2025 briefing gives 50 h of hibernation on the battery; the team chose the mission limit.

sources.label: NASA, VIPER Industry Day technical briefing (Feb 2025)
NASA, Blue Origin to deliver VIPER
